label: techtree-full-n3
_why: THE FIRST FULL-LENGTH LOOK AT THE MOD WITH ITS TECH TREE (ROADMAP step 4, first pass). Four questions, all of which need a whole campaign rather than a probe: (1) GDP sizes and their trajectory; (2) the TECHNOLOGY PICTURE BY DECADE - how far up a 217-technology tree countries actually get, which is the thing the deeper tree and the spread boost were tuned against and which no static analysis can answer; (3) whether a hundred years is STABLE - no CTD, no runaway error growth, no economy collapse; (4) WALL CLOCK, because a deeper tree plus 38 more technologies plus 33 more buildings is a real performance question and the answer decides whether this design is playable at all.
_arm: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.json} - the full modded build, n=3. NOT a control. Three runs because a single campaign is one RNG draw and the questions above are all distributional; three is what tells a trend from a fluke without costing a second night.
_comparison: ⚠ THIS BATCH CARRIES NO VANILLA ARM, so 'compared to vanilla averages' cannot be answered from it alone. Vanilla references must come from an earlier vanilla session or a follow-up batch, and any finding written from this data must say which. Adding three vanilla runs here would have doubled a ~5h batch to ~10h.
_metrics: country_state gives per-country GDP + foreign-owned GDP + market, and with `population` on it also carries workforce composition - which is the sharpest test in ROADMAP step 4 (runners-up should hold far fewer engineers, machinists and capitalists). tech_log gives every acquisition by every country to the day, which IS the tech-picture-by-decade answer. building_inventory gives what actually got built.
_cost: 3 runs x 100 in-game years. At roughly a minute per in-game year plus ~40s load, MEASURED on the first attempt: ~0.68 in-game years per minute early on, and late game is slower still, so budget ~2.5-3.5h per run and ~8h for the batch. The first launch used timeout_minutes 200 and was stopped and relaunched at 330 before it could guillotine a run at 1900 - an established long-run schedule in this repo uses 260 for 85 years.
